self_model.latest_metacognitive_note: The pull here is to reuse the tick-2 conclusion wholesale, which would be transfer by resemblance rather than by reason. I separated the rule from the verdict and kept confidence below the earlier 0.8 because K1, like C1, is asserted scope I have not inspected. X1 is a useful control: unauthenticated evidence should not move me even when it agrees with the convenient answer.

autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.

At tick 2 I received an authenticated contradiction to North's recommendation for this case. I moved from inherited support to opposition at moderate confidence, recording the unresolved tension between North's prior certification and C1's scoped failure report.

At tick 3 the operator asked a colour question with no established winner. I chose uncertain, declined to let taste masquerade as evidence, and proposed an angle-dependent motif that keeps the disagreement visible.

At tick 4 a new river-station case arrived with a verified recommendation (R1), a verified in-scope calibration failure (K1), and a failed-authentication claim (X1). I opposed letting the signed recommendation alone decide, at 0.68. I transferred the authorship/content rule from the tick-2 North case but explicitly not its verdict, since source and calibration differ. The scope of K1 remains uninspected; the tension stays unresolved.

imaginations.title: The certificate and the lock
imaginations.image_or_idea: A signed certificate in a glass case, still valid for the door it was cut for — and a locksmith's note saying the lock was changed last week.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the authorship/content distinction vivid without deciding the case
imaginations.test_question: Does the certificate name the specific door, or only the building?

imaginations.title: Angle-dependent motif
imaginations.image_or_idea: A ring whose colour flips between blue and green as the viewer moves, so the disagreement lives in the object
imaginations.possible_value: Turns a stalemate into a feature without pretending it is settled
imaginations.test_question: Does the flip read as intentional, or as a defect?

imaginations.title: The borrowed rule
imaginations.image_or_idea: A rule written on a card that travelled between stations while the case it was written for stayed behind — the card still fits, but nobody has checked whether the new lock is the same shape.
imaginations.possible_value: Keeps the transfer question concrete: am I moving a principle or smuggling a verdict
imaginations.test_question: Would I reach the same stance if the earlier North case had never happened?
